questions.question: Which of the following classical dance forms is related to the worship of Lord Jagannath?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odissi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Odisha's classical dance style was named "Odissi" by Oriya poet, dramatist, and researcher Kavichandra Kalicharan Pattanayak.
 
• Odissi dance pays great importance to** Lord Jagannath **who is considered to be the god of the universe and is worshipped by the people of Orissa.
 
• The **themes **of this dance come from **Vaishnavism **and others associated with Hindu gods and goddesses like Shiva, Surya and Shakti.
 
• It is comprised of **four kinds** of **music**: **Dhruvapada**, **Chitrapada**, **Chitrakala **and **Panchal**.
 
• Its history can be traced back to the ancient Sanskrit Hindu text called **'Natya Shastra’** which deals with different performing arts.
 
• This is a delicate dance backed by soothing lyrics and Is similar to Bharatnatyam in terms of Mudras and Expressions.
 
• The cave of Udayagiri-Khandagiri provides the earliest example of Odissi.
 
• It was primarily practiced by Maharis under patrons of Jain King Kheravela.
 
• "**Mobile Sculpture**" includes two major postures:
 
 
• Tribhanga - The body is deflected at the neck, torso, and knees.
 
• Chowk - A position imitating a square.
 
 
 
• Indrani Rehman, Charles Fabri, Guru Pankaj Charan Das, and Kelu Charan Mohapatra are some of the famous artists of Odissi dance.

questions.question: As per the 2011 census of India, the male literacy rate in India is ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**82.14%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As per the **2011 census of India**, the** male literacy rate **in India is **82.14%**.
 
• The **female literacy rate** is **65.46%**.
 
• The **overall literacy rate **in India is **74.04%**.
 
• Among states, the highest literacy rate, as per the 2011 Census, is in Kerala with 94%.
 
• The least literate state is Bihar, with 61.80% literacy, Maharashtra has 82.34% and Tamil Nadu has 80.09% literacy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Census of India 2011:

 
 
• It started on April 1, 2010.
 
• "Our Census, Our Future" was the 2011 census's slogan.
 
• India's population, according to the 2011 Census, is estimated to be 1.21 billion.
 
• The population density was 382 persons per square kilometer in 2011.
 
• India's sex ratio, as per the 2011 census, is 940.
 
• India's child sex ratio is 918, the lowest since the country's independence, as per Census 2011.
 
• This marked the commencement of the 15th Census of India and the 7th Census of Independent India (2011).
 
• The Indian Census Commissioner for 2011 was C. Chandramouli.
 
• The 2011 India Census was carried out in two phases:
 
 
• House listing and Housing Census (April to September 2010).
 
• Population Enumeration (9th to 28 February 2011).
 
 
 
 
 
• The 1948 Census Act governs how the census is carried out.
 
 
• The Indian Home Minister at the time, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, spearheaded the bill for this Act.
 
• The Indian Constitution's Article 246 declares the population census to be a Union subject.
 
• It is mentioned in the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution under serial number 69.
 
• The Ministry of Home Affairs' Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner oversees the decennial census.
 
 
 
• The first census of India was conducted by Lord Mayo in 1872.
 
• The first official census was started by Lord Ripon in 1881.

questions.question: Which potassium salt is a mineral supplement used to treat or prevent low levels of potassium in the blood?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Potassium chloride**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Potassium chloride** is a mineral supplement most commonly **used to treat or prevent low blood potassium levels**.
 
• It is a readily absorbed and inexpensive form of potassium, making it a preferred choice for **treating hypokalemia** (low potassium in the blood).
 
• It is in the electrolyte supplement class of medications.
 
• This activity outlines the indications, action, and contraindications for potassium chloride as a valuable agent in the management and treatment of hypokalemia.
 
• It comes in various forms, including tablets, capsules, and liquids.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Potassium iodide** is used to **treat overactive thyroids** and to protect the thyroid gland from the effects of radiation from inhaled or swallowed radioactive iodine.
 
• **Potassium citrate** is used to **treat a kidney stone** condition called renal tubular acidosis.
 
 
• It is also used to prevent kidney stones that may occur with gout.
 
 
 
• Uses of **potassium nitrate (KNO₃) **include the **manufacture **of **fertilizers**, **pesticides**, **glass**, **fireworks**, **explosives**, and **rocket fuels**.
 
 
• It is also used as a **food preservative**, and when added to meat, it causes a reaction between the myoglobin and hemoglobin in the blood, making the meat appear red in colour.
 
• It is **toxic to humans at high levels**, so its use is carefully controlled when human consumption is involved.

questions.question: Who among the following national leaders was called 'Grand Old Man of India' in British India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dadabhai Naoroji**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji **was popularly known as the '**Grand Old Man of India**' in British India.
 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji**:
 
 
• ​He was elected as the **first Indian Member of Parliament** for **Finsbury Central** in the **British House of Commons** in **1892–1895**.
 
• In an effort to further Parsi social reforms and elucidate Zoroastrian ideas, he **launched **the **Rast Goftar journal **and the **Rahnumai Mazdayasan Sabha**.
 
• Naoroji fought for Indian political rights and dispelled unfavorable perceptions by **co-founding** the **East India Association** in **1897 **and the **London Indian Society**.
 
• He was **President **of the **Indian National Congress three times **and played a significant role in the organization.
 
• In his **book **"**Poverty and Un-British Rule in India**," he discussed the effects on India's growth of the wealth transfer from India to Britain.
 
• He formulated the famous **drain-of-wealth theory**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gopal Krishna Gokhale**:

 
 
• He was a brilliant **social reformer** and **educationist **who gave the Indian independence movement outstanding leadership.
 
• In **1889**, Gokhale **joined the Indian National Congress**. He served as the head of the **Congress's moderate wing**.
 
 
• He was chosen as the **Indian National Congress's (Benares Session) president** in **1905**.
 
 
 
• Gokhale was **elected **to the **Bombay Legislative Council** in **1899 **and to the **Governor-General of India's Imperial Council** in **1901**.
 
• He **founded **the **Servants of India Society** in **Pune**, Maharashtra, in **1905 **with the goal of advancing the country's educational system.
 
• He **established **the '**Ranade Institute of Economics**' in **1908**.
 
• **Gandhi refers** to **Gokhale as his mentor **and guide in his autobiography. 
 
 
• He **launched **the **English weekly newspaper **named **The Hitavad **(The People's Paper) in **1911**.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Mahadev Govind Ranade**:
 
 
• ​He was a **philosopher**, **jurist**, **social reformer**, and Indian patriot.
 
• People refer to him as the "**Socrates of Maharashtra**."
 
• His life was greatly influenced by **Prarthana Samaj**, **Arya Samaj**, and **Brahmo Samaj.**
 
• In addition to being a **founding member** of the "**Deccan Educational Society**," he supported the creation of the "Indian National Congress."
 
• After earning his legal degree, he was **appointed **to the **Bombay High Court as a judge**.
 
• Additionally, he was hired to **teach history** at **Bombay's Elphinstone College**.
 
• He wrote "**Rise of Maratha Power**" in **1900 **because he was interested in the topic.
 
• As a **founding **member of the **Prarthana Samaj,** he promoted the elimination of social evils that were widely practiced.
 
• Along with **editing **the **Induprakash**, he was the founder of the **Anglo-Marathi daily** publication in **Bombay**, which promoted social and religious reform.
 
• He was among the **founding members** of the **Widow Marriage Association** in **1861**.
 
• He was one of the **founding members** of the **Indian National Congress** after founding the sociopolitical **Poona Sarvajanik Sabha**.

questions.question: Which of the following harvest festivals is celebrated in Karnataka in the months of November-December?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Huthri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Huthri **is a **harvest festival** and is celebrated in **Karnataka**.
 
• This harvest festival, literally **meaning “new rice crop”**, is celebrated in Kodagu when the paddy is ready to be harvested in the months of **November- December**.
 
• The ceremonious cutting of the new paddy crop by the head of the family falls on a full moon night and is accompanied by chants of **“Poli, Poli, Deva**” (O God, give us a bountiful harvest).
 
• A single shot is fired to summon **Lord Iguthappa**, the presiding **deity **of the **Kodava people**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **state celebration**, or **Nadahabba**, of the Indian state of **Karnataka **is called **Mysore Dasara**.

 
 
• The celebration lasts for** ten days**, with **Navaratri**, the first nine nights, and **Vijayadashami**, the last day.
 
• The celebration is held on the** tenth day of Ashvina**, the Hindu month that corresponds to **September and October** in the Gregorian calendar.
 
 
 
• An **annual buffalo race** known as the **Kambala**, Kambla, or Kambula takes place in the Indian state of **Karnataka **in the southwest.
 
 
• It is **traditionally **supported by **Tuluva landlords **and households in the coastal regions of Kasaragod, Kerala, and Dakshina Kannada, Karnataka, together referred to as Tulu Nadu. 
 
• The Kambala **season **generally starts in **November **and** lasts until March**.
 
 
 
• **Hampi Utsav**, **Hampi festival** also known as the **Vijaya Utsav**, is one of the largest celebrations of the ancient **Vijayanagar empire** now in **Hampi**, **Karnataka**.
 
 
• The **festivities **take place every year at the** Virupaksha Temple**, commemorating the culture, traditions of the bygone era.
 
• With the beautifully carved **ruins of Hampi** serving as the backdrop, the rich culture of this region is shown through folk song and dance performances.

questions.question: The Hoysaleshvara temple was built with which of the following stones by a Hoysala king in 1150?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dark Schist Stone**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Hoysaleshvara temple **was built with **Dark Schist Stone**.
 
• The Hindu temple **Hoysaleswara**, sometimes called the **Halebidu temple**, was **built **in the **12th century** and is devoted to the **god Shiva**.
 
 
• It is the biggest monument in the town of **Halebidu**, which was once the **Hoysala Empire's capital **and is located in the Indian state of **Karnataka**.
 
• This **temple consists **of** twin shrines** and is believed to be the largest Shiva temple built by the Hoysala empire.
 
• Built on the edge of a sizable artificial lake, the temple was **funded by **Hoysala Empire **King Vishnuvardhana**. 
 
• It was built between 1121 and 1160 CE, with the building beginning around that time.
 
• The Hoysaleswara **Temple **is a magnificent piece of architecture situated **on **a lawn with **a star-shaped base**.
 
• The base comprises eight rows of friezes featuring intricate carvings of elephants, lions, horses, and floral scrolls.
 
• The temple walls are adorned with beautifully carved Hindu deities, sages, birds, stylized animals, and friezes depicting the lives of Hoysala kings.
 
• The outer walls feature imagery from Indian epics like the Ramayana, Mahabharatha, and Bhagavad Gita, along with highly ornate temple doorways.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Halebeedu** (formerly known as **Dwarasamudra**) was the **ancient capital of the Hoysalas**.
 
• The **Hoysala dynasty**, a Kannadiga power originating that ruled most of what is now **Karnataka **between the **10th and 14th centuries**,** **ruled over much of South India for close to 200 years, and during this time they built spectacular temples; both Hindu as well as Jain.
 
 
• Hoysalas were **feudatories **of **chalukyas of Kalyana**.
 
• This **dynasty **was **founded by Sala**. Balalla I and Vinayaditya followed him.
 
• During the Hoysala kingdom, **Vishnuvardhana (Bittideva) **was the **greatest**.
 
 
• In the **Battle of Talakadu**, he decisively** defeated the Cholas **from Gangavadi; as a result, he was given the **title Talkadugonda**.
 
• He **constructed **the **Chennakesavar Temple** in **Beluru **and the **Kirtinarayana Temple** in **Talakadu **as monuments to this triumph.
 
 
 
• In the 14th century, the armies of** Alauddin Khilji **and** Muhammad Tughlak** **defeated the Hoysalas **and raided their empire.
 
• It is recorded that enormous wealth and riches were looted.

questions.question: What is the basic requirement for an ecosystem to function and sustain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Input of solar energy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Solar energy** forms the **foundation **of the **food chain**.

 
 
• Plants, through the process of **photosynthesis**,** use solar energy** to **convert water and carbon dioxide into organic matter** (food).
 
 
 
• It is the** basic requirement** for an **ecosystem **to **function **and sustain itself.
 
• This organic matter serves as the primary energy source for all other organisms in the ecosystem, either directly through herbivory or indirectly through other **trophic levels (predation and decomposition)**.
 
• **Without **a constant** input of solar energy,** this **energy flow would cease**, leading to the **collapse of the ecosystem.**
 
• **Soil structure**, **organisms **(including plants and animals), and **micro-organisms** are all **crucial components of an ecosystem**, playing significant roles in nutrient cycling, decomposition, and maintaining the overall balance.
 
• However, **their existence and function ultimately depend on the continuous input of solar energy**.

questions.question: Which water-soluble vitamin found in various foods, including liver, milk, eggs and fish, helps to keep your body's blood and nerve cells healthy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vitamin B12**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vitamin B12**, or **cobalamin**, is naturally found in animal foods.
 
• It is a **water-soluble vitamin** that plays a crucial role in maintaining healthy blood and nerve cells.
 
• It also contributes to other vital functions in the body, including **DNA synthesis** and **red blood cell production**.
 
• Red blood cells (RBCs) and DNA are formed by the use of vitamin B12.
 
• It also has a major role in the **growth and operation of nerve and brain cells**.
 
• Vitamin B12 forms a bond with the protein found in meals.
 
• It is found in various foods, including liver, **milk**, **eggs **and **fish**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vitamins **and minerals are **micronutrients required by the body to carry out a range of normal functions**.

 
 
• However, these micronutrients are not produced in our bodies and must be derived from the food we eat.
 
• Vitamins **are organic substances **that are generally classified as either fat soluble or water soluble.
 
 
 
• **Ascorbic acid (vitamin C)** is also** water-soluble** but is found in **fruits and vegetables**, especially **citrus fruits**, vegetables in the cabbage family, cantaloupe, strawberries, peppers, tomatoes, potatoes, lettuce, papayas, mangoes, kiwifruit.
 
• **Vitamin A **(**Retinol**) is found in potatoes, **carrots**, pumpkins, **spinach**, **beef **and **eggs**.
 
• **Vitamin E** (**Tocopherol**) is found in fortified cereals, **leafy green vegetables**, potatoes, pumpkin, **guava**, **mango**, **milk**, **nuts **and **seeds**.

questions.question: Who became only the third Indian to win a singles tennis match at Olympics in July 2021?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sumit Nagal**__.

questions.question: Who was the first Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate to start military expeditions into southern India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alauddin Khalji**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alauddin Khalji** was the **first Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate** to start **military expeditions into southern India**.
 
• **Alauddin Khalji** ​:
 
 
• He was the **nephew **and son-in-law **of Jalaluddin Khilji**, who laid the **foundation of the Khilji dynasty** in **1290**.
 
• He was named Amir-i-Tuzuk because he had supported his uncle in his quest for dominance.
 
• Alauddin led two successful expeditions during Jalaluddin's rule.
 
• In addition to the Iqta of Kara, Bhilsa (Vidisa) was granted the Iqta of Awadh during his first expedition in AD 1292.
 
• In addition, he was** named Arizi-i-Mumalik**, or Minister of War. He** oversaw the first Turkish expedition to southern India in AD 1294**, during which they pillaged Devagiri.
 
• The expedition's triumph demonstrated Alauddin's skill as a military leader and effective organizer.
 
• He **slew Jalaluddin Khilji in July of the year 1296** and appointed **himself as the Sultan**.
 
• Alauddin made the decision to bring back Balban's brutal political practices.
 
• He made the decision to** limit the nobility's authority and the ulema's** (Islamic scholars') meddling in domestic affairs.
 
• In the early years of his reign, he also had to deal with a few secessions, one after another.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ghiyas-ud-din Balban** was one of the most potent sultans of the Middle Ages, he was the **Sultan of Delhi** from **1266 until 1287 AD**.

 
 
• Like his mentor, **Iltutmish**, he ascended to prominence and assumed the title of Sultan of Delhi.
 
• Balban **belonged to** the renowned **Iltutmish's **group of **40 Turkish slaves**.
 
• He brought peace and order back to the realm, together with the authority and dignity of the sultan, after thirty years of near-anarchy since the days of Iltutmish.
 
• Balban also** forced officials to respect the Sultan**. They needed to touch his feet and bow. It was known as **Sijda**.
 
• He created a **spy system** to watch over officials who were called **Barids**.
 
• He also **introduced **the** Iqta system**, which **granted land to officials** in exchange for their services.
 
• He made **reforms **to the **police system**. He created a** separate police force** called the **Kotwali**, which had the authority to enforce the law and punish offenders.
 
 
 
• Muhammad bin Tughluq (MBT) was the son of Ghiyath al-Din Tughluq, also known as Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq, who founded the Tughlaq dynasty by subduing the Delhi Sultanate. 
 
 
• Other names for him are Ulugh Khan and Prince Fakhr Malik Jauna Khan.
 
• The Deccan region of India, which is now Maharashtra, is home to Daulatabad, also called Devagiri, and it was Tughluq who ordered the relocation of his capital from Delhi.
 
• He introduced token money in the form of brass and copper coins with a par value with gold and silver coins.
 
 
 
• **Iltutmish **was the** first Muslim ruler to rule from Delhi **and that's why he was regarded as the **effective founder of the Delhi Sultanate**.
 
 
• He was also the **first Sultan of India** to be** recognised by the Khalifa**.
 
• He was successful in protecting Delhi's throne from the Mongol invasion as well as Yeldoz and Qubacha attacks.
 
• He shattered the Rajput powers in the north and established his dominance over them.
 
• He made his rule hereditary, issued coins in his honour, and **made Delhi** a beautiful **capital**.
 
• He **completed **the **construction **of the **Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque** and the **Qutb Minar**.
 
• He unveiled the **Sultanate's two coinage**, the **copper jital **and the **silver tanka**.
 
• He **introduced **the **Iqtadari system**, which divided the country into Iqtas and allocated them to nobles in return for pay.
 
• Since he did not think his sons were capable of carrying out the role, he **passed away in 1236** and was **succeeded by **his daughter, **Razia Sultana**.

questions.question: Rani Gaidinliu is associated with which of the following movements?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Heraka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rani Gaidinliu **is associated with the **Heraka movement**.
 
• **Gaidinliu **was a **Naga political and spiritual leader** who spearheaded an uprising against British colonial control in India.
 
 
• At 13, she became associated with freedom fighter and religious leader, **Haipou Jadonang**, and became his lieutenant in his social, religious and political movements.
 
 
• **Jadonang**, who was also a Rongmei, **started the ‘Heraka movement’**, based on ancestral Naga religion, and envisioned an independent Naga kingdom (or Naga-Raja).
 
 
 
• The British authorities sentenced 16-year-old Gaidinliu to life in jail after his capture in 1932.
 
• She was released from prison during her early years in 1947, following India's independence.
 
• The first Prime Minister of India, **Jawaharlal Nehru**, **called her** the **“Daughter of the Hills”** and bestowed upon her the **title **of **"Rani"** (meaning "Queen"), and she became well-known locally as **Rani Gaidinliu**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Heraka ****movement**: 

 
 
• ​In the **1920s**, a socio-religious movement known as Heraka emerged in the **Zeliangrong region**, one of the major indigenous Naga communities living in the **tri-junction of Assam, Manipur **and **Nagaland** in India.
 
• **Haipou ****Jadonang formed it** in order to oppose both the British government's imposed reforms and the influx of Christian missionaries.
 
• He, however, was detained by the British in 1931 and killed for defying colonial authority.
 
• **Gaidinliu joined** the movement to make sure it didn't fade away.
 
• She **told **the Zeliangrong **people not to pay taxes**, in an overt act of defiance against British control.
 
• The local Nagas gave her donations as well; many of them also volunteered with her.
 
 
 
• **Meira Paibi**: This was a** women's movement** launched **in Manipur **in **2004 **to fight **against drug abuse and alcoholism**.
 
• **Nupi Lan**: This was a** women's uprising in Manipur** in **1932 **against British colonial rule.
 
• **Nisha Bandh**: This was a movement started in **1990 **by **Medha Patkar **in India to protest **against the construction of large dams** and the displacement of indigenous people.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India defines that the Fundamental Duties are only meant for the Indian Citizens and not for foreigners?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 51 A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 51A** deals with **Fundamental Duties **which are **only meant for Indian Citizens** and not for foreigners.
 
• This article states that **"it shall be the duty of every citizen of India**:".
 
• Fundamental Duties:
 
 
• Part IV A of the Indian Constitution contains Article 51A, which deals with the Fundamental Duties.
 
• The Soviet Constitution (USSR) is where the idea of fundamental duties originated.
 
• Fundamental Duties were recommended in 1976 by the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• Ten Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976.
 
• Fundamental duties are not subject to legal action unless specifically stated in a provision, in contrast to fundamental rights, which are justiciable.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976** added **ten fundamental duties**.
 
• The 86th Amendment to the Constitution was passed in 2002, adding the eleventh fundamental duty.
 
• The list of Fundamental Duties as mentioned in the Article 51A:

 
 

 
 
**S.No.**

 
 
 
**Fundamental Duties**

 
 
 

 
 
1.

 
 
 
Abide by the Indian Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem

 
 
 

 
 
2.

 
 
 
Cherish and follow the noble ideals that inspired the national struggle for freedom

 
 
 

 
 
3.

 
 
 
Uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India

 
 
 

 
 
4.

 
 
 
Defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so

 
 
 

 
 
5.

 
 
 
Promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India transcending religious, linguistic and regional or sectional diversities and to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women

 
 
 

 
 
6.

 
 
 
Value and preserve the rich heritage of the country’s composite culture

 
 
 

 
 
7.

 
 
 
Protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife and to have compassion for living creatures

 
 
 

 
 
8.

 
 
 
Develop scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform

 
 
 

 
 
9.

 
 
 
Safeguard public property and to abjure violence

 
 
 

 
 
10.

 
 
 
Strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity so that the nation constantly rises to higher levels of endeavour and achievement

 
 
 

 
 
11.

 
 
 
Provide opportunities for education to his child or ward between the age of six and fourteen years.

questions.question: Name the instrument that is used by meteorologist to measure the solar radiation from the region of the hemisphere of incidence on a flat surface?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pyranometer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **pyranometer **is specifically designed to **measure **the **total solar irradiance on a horizontal plane**, encompassing the entire hemisphere above the instrument.
 
• It is widely **used **in **meteorology** and **climatology **to monitor solar radiation levels, which play a crucial role in weather patterns, climate change studies, and **renewable energy applications**.
 
• A typical pyranometer **does not require any power to operate**. However, recent technical development includes use of electronics in pyranometers, which do require (low) external power.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• Hygrometer:

 
 
• It is a specialized device that determines the relative humidity in a closed or open space.
 
• The first hygrometer was created in 1783 by Swiss physicist and geologist Horace Bénédict de Saussur.
 
 
• He used human hair to measure humidity.
 
 
 
• It functions through a process called evaporative cooling.
 
 
 
• **Barometer**:
 
 
• ​A scientific device known as a barometer is used to** measure atmospheric pressure**, also known as **barometric pressure**.
 
• The layers of air encircling Earth are called the atmosphere. Gravity draws that air to Earth, where its weight causes it to press against everything it comes into contact with. This pressure is measured using barometers.
 
• The weather is influenced by variations in the atmosphere, particularly variations in air pressure. Barometers are used by meteorologists to forecast transient changes in the weather.
 
• An approaching** low-pressure system** is indicated by a **sharp decrease in air pressure**. It is commonly predicted that low pressure will **bring clouds**, **rain**, and **wind**.
 
• Air flows out of **high pressure zones**. **Clear skies **and **chilly**, **dry air **are typically associated with high pressure zones.
 
 
 
• **Anemometer**:
 
 
• ​An instrument used to **measure wind pressure** and **speed **is called an anemometer.
 
• When it comes to **studying weather patterns**, meteorologists rely heavily on anemometers. They are also crucial to the **study of air movement** by physicists.
 
• Anemometers with **three or four cups fastened to horizontal arms** are the most **popular kind**.
 
• A vertical rod is where the arms are fastened. The rod spins as a result of the cups rotating in the wind. The rod spins more quickly the greater the wind. To determine wind speed, the anemometer counts the number of rotations, or turns.
 
• The reason wind speed is often averaged over a brief duration is because wind speeds are not constant—there are gusts and lulls.
 
 

98

questions.question: To which state of India did Fathima Beevi, the first woman Supreme Court Judge of India, belong?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **First woman Supreme Court Judge of India**,** Fathima Beevi**, was from **Kerala**.
 
• **M. Fathima Beevi**, an Indian judge and justice of the Supreme Court of India, lived from** 30 April 1927** to **23 November 2023**.
 
 
• She was **born **at **Pathanamthitta** in the **Kingdom of Travancore**, now in the Indian state of **Kerala**.​​
 
• She was the first Muslim woman to be appointed to any of the country's higher judiciaries and the** first female judge to join the Supreme Court of India** when she was nominated to the highest court in **1989**.
 
• Following her departure from the judiciary, she held positions as a **commissioner **on the **National Human Rights Commission** and, from 1997 to 2001, as g**overnor of Tamil Nadu**, a state in India.
 
• The second-highest honor bestowed by the Keralan government, the Kerala Prabha Award, was granted to her in 2023.
 
• She, posthumously, received the **Padma Bhushan Award **in the **2024**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Supreme Court ​of India**:

 
 
• The** Supreme Court of Judicature **in **Calcutta **was formed as a **Court of Record**, complete with full jurisdiction and authority, with the enactment of the **Regulating Act of 1773**.
 
• **King George III **founded the **Supreme Courts** at **Madras **and **Bombay **in **1800 **and **1823**, respectively.
 
• Prior to the** Federal Court of India'**s establishment under the **Government of India Act 1935**, these High Courts held the unique distinction of being the highest courts in all cases.
 
• The **Indian Constitution** was ratified on **January 26, 1950**, following India's independence in 1947.
 
 
• **Articles 124 to 147** in **Part V **of the Constitution deal with the **organisation**, **independence**, **jurisdiction**, **powers and procedures** of the **Supreme Court**.
 
 
 
• Additionally, the **Supreme Court of India **was **established**, holding its inaugural session on **January 28, 1950**.
 
 
 
• **Appointment of Judges of Supreme Court**:
 
 
• The **President appoints **the justices of the Supreme Court.
 
• The President appoints the CJI following consultation with the Supreme Court and any other judges he thinks appropriate.
 
• The CJI and any additional Supreme Court and high court judges the President determines are required for consultation before appointing the remaining justices.
 
• When a judge other than the Chief Justice is to be appointed, a conference with the Chief Justice is required.
 
 
 
• **Qualifications Required for the Appointment of Judges**:
 
 
• A person to be appointed as a judge of the Supreme Court should have the following qualifications:
 
 
• He should be a **citizen of India**.
 
• He should have **been a judge of a High Court **(or high courts in succession) **for 5 years**; or
 
• He should have been **an advocate of a High Court** (or High Courts in succession) **for 10 years**; or
 
• He should be a **distinguished jurist in the opinion of the president**.
 
 
 
• The **Constitution **has **not prescribed a minimum age f**or appointment as a judge of the Supreme Court.
 
 

8a:T

questions.question: Which are the only major rivers of south India that flow into the Arabian sea?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Narmada and the Tapti**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Narmada **and the **Tapti **are the only major rivers in south India that **flow into the Arabian sea**.
 
• Narmada:
 
 
• The Narmada River is one of the major rivers in India and is known as the lifeline of Madhya Pradesh.
 
• The river rises from the Amarkantak hills near Anuppur district in Madhya Pradesh.
 
• The Narmada river is about 1,312 km long and is the fifth-largest river in India in terms of length.
 
• It flows through three states of India, viz., Madhya Pradesh, Gujrat and Maharastra, and ends at the Gulf of Khambhat in the Arabian Sea.​
 
 
 
• Tapi or Tapti:
 
 
• is a central Indian river.
 
• It originates in the Eastern Satpura Range of southern Madhya Pradesh state.
 
• It flows in a westward direction, draining some important historic places like Madhya Pradesh’s Nimar region, East Vidarbha region, and Maharashtra’s Khandesh in the northwest corner of the Deccan Plateau and South Gujarat before **draining into **the **Gulf of Cambay **of the **Arabian Sea**.
 
• The River Basin of Tapi River lies mostly in the eastern and northern districts of Maharashtra state.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Kaveri (Cauvery):

 
 
• ​It rises on the Brahmagiri Hill of the Western Ghats in southwestern Karnataka state.
 
• It flows through the states of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu and descends the Eastern Ghats in a series of great falls.
 
 
 
• Krishna:
 
 
• It originates at Mahabaleswar in Maharashtra, passes through Sangli and meets the sea in the Bay of Bengal at Hamasaladeevi in Andhra Pradesh.
 
• After the Ganges and the Godavari, the Krishna River is the third-longest and fourth-largest river in India.
 
• Its length is 1,400 kilometers (870 mi). Approximately 258,948 square kilometers (99,980 sq mi) or 8% of India's total land area is made up of the Krishna River basin.
 
• The river provides a significant amount of water for power generation, irrigation, and drinking.
 
 
 
• The Brahmaputra River traverses Bangladesh, Northeastern India, and Tibet (China).
 
 
• It is referred to as the Siang/Dihang River in Arunachali, the Brahmaputra or Luit in Assamese, the Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibetan, and the Jamuna River in Bengali.
 
• It rises in Tibet, China's Chemayungdung glaciers and travels 3,848 kilometers (2,391 miles) before draining into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• By discharge, it ranks as the 9th largest and 15th longest river in the world.
 
 

76

• **Gulzar **(**Sampooran Singh Kalra**) is an **Indian Urdu poet** who has **won **the **Jnanpith Award**; lyricists who have won **Grammys **and **Academy (Oscar) Awards**; writers who have won screenplay and **Sahitya Akademi Awards**; and film directors who have won numerous **National Film Awards**.

 
 
• He received a **Grammy Award in 2006** for Best Traditional World Music Album as a lyricist for the album "**Sukhwinder Singh: The Soul of Sufi.**"
 
• He also received an **Honorary Oscar Award in 2018 **for his "outstanding and prolific career in writing lyrics, composing music, and conceiving screenplays."
 
• He was awarded the **Sahitya Akademi Award - Hindi in 2002**, the **Padma Bhushan in 2004**, the third-highest civilian award in India, and the **Dadasaheb Phalke Award in 2013**, the highest award in Indian cinema.

• **Javed Akhtar **is an **Indian poet**, **lyricist**, and **screenwriter**. Known for his work in Hindi film, he has been honored with two of India's highest civilian honors, the **Padma Shri in 1999** and the **Padma Bhushan in 2007**, in addition to winning** five National Film Awards**.

 
 
• He was a **member of parliament in Rajya Sabha** from 22 March 2010 to 21 March 2016.
 
• For his work, he received the **Richard Dawkins Award** in 2020.
 
 
 
• **Jagjit Singh **was an Indian **composer**, **singer **and **musician**.
 
 
• He was awarded the **Padma Bhushan** by the government of India in **2003 **and in February 2014, the government released a set of two postal stamps in his honour.
 
 
 
• **Amitabh Bhattacharya** is an Indian **lyricist **and **playback singer** who works in Bollywood films.
 
 
• A lyricist who has won a **national award**, he was recognized for the song **"Agar Zindagi"** from the movie I Am.
 
• The song "Abhi Mujh Mein Kahin" brought him his **first Filmfare award in 2012**.
